name: Japan
summary: Japan taxes gains on listed shares and listed-company dividends separately at 20.315% (15.315% national including reconstruction surtax plus 5% local), but for 2025 and 2026 a minimum tax of 22.5% applies to aggregate income above JPY 330 million, and from 2027 the threshold is JPY 165 million at 30% (per PwC), so very large realised gains face more. There is no wealth tax. Inheritance and gift tax is among the world's highest: 10% to 55% on each heir's statutory share above a basic deduction of JPY 30 million plus 6 million per statutory heir. Foreigners on working-type visas who have lived in Japan 10 years or less in the last 15 are taxed only on Japanese assets at death, and for the first 5 years non-permanent residents are taxed on foreign income only if it is paid in or remitted to Japan. An exit tax applies to departing residents with JPY 100 million or more of securities.

regimes.name: Permanent resident taxpayer (Japanese national, or foreigner resident more than 5 of the last 10 years)
regimes.description: Worldwide income; separate 20.315% taxation of listed share gains and listed dividends; worldwide inheritance tax once the foreigner thresholds are passed.
regimes.eligibility: Resident with a domicile (jusho) in Japan or a residence for 1 year or more; permanent-resident taxpayer status for a foreigner after more than 5 years of stay in the last 10. Worldwide inheritance tax for a foreigner after more than 10 of the last 15 years (or with a permanent-type visa).

capital_gains.summary: Gains on listed shares are taxed separately at 20.315% (income tax 15% + 2.1% reconstruction surtax on it + 5% local inhabitant tax). Unlisted shares are also taxed separately at 20.315%, and listed and unlisted losses cannot offset each other. Real estate: 20.315% if held more than 5 years at 1 January of the sale year, 39.63% if shorter. Minimum tax on high earners: for 2025 and 2026, 22.5% of aggregate income (including separately taxed gains) above JPY 330 million, charged to the extent it exceeds regular tax; per PwC, from 2027 the threshold falls to JPY 165 million and the rate rises to 30%.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: NISA tax-free accounts (limited amounts, not relevant at this scale). Minimum tax threshold JPY 330 million (2025-2026).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Exit tax (Income Tax Act art. 60-2; NTA Tax Answer 1478): residents who lived in Japan more than 5 of the last 10 years and hold JPY 100 million or more of securities and similar assets are deemed to sell them on departure; payment can be deferred 5 (up to 10) years with a tax agent and collateral. Gifts or bequests of such assets to non-residents trigger the same deemed sale.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Separate taxation at 15.315% national + 5% local = 20.315% for listed and unlisted shares and long-term real estate. Foreign listed shares through a Japanese broker are taxed the same way. Not modelled: the minimum tax, which lifts the effective rate towards 22.5% on income far above JPY 330 million (2025-2026) and towards 30% above JPY 165 million from 2027.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Share gains of individuals remain separately taxed at 20.315% even for active traders; business-scale trading of other assets falls into aggregate income (top about 55.945%).
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: Real estate: more than 5 years (counted to 1 January of the year of sale) for 20.315%, otherwise 39.63%. No holding period for shares.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Permanent residents are taxed on worldwide gains with a foreign tax credit. Foreign asset report required above JPY 50 million (not verified).

dividends.summary: Dividends are in principle aggregate income (top about 55.945%, with a small dividend credit for Japanese dividends), but dividends from listed companies (shareholders under 3%) can be taxed separately at 20.315%, which is final. Foreign listed dividends received through a Japanese payer are taxed at 20.315% after foreign withholding, with a foreign tax credit available by filing.
dividends.important_exceptions: Holders of 3% or more of a listed company, and owners of unlisted companies, are taxed at aggregate rates up to about 55.945% on dividends (minus dividend credit).

dividends.rate_basis: Listed portfolio dividends: separate taxation 20.315% (domestic and foreign listed). Headline = aggregate top rate 45% x 1.021 + 10% = 55.945% for non-listed/large holdings.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 20.42% on dividends to non-residents (15.315% for listed dividends to portfolio holders), reduced by treaty.
dividends.treaty_network: Broad network covering the US, EU and Asian partners (count not verified).
dividends.holding_company_notes: Modelled as the structure regime 'asset_management_kk' (a Japanese KK or GK holding the portfolio): about 35.43% effective on all income at the top (Tokyo, small company), no 95% exclusion for portfolio dividends, 20% exclusion for domestic dividends on stakes of 5% or less, foreign withholding creditable; profits paid out are taxed to the family at about 49.4% after the dividend credit. Against 20.315% for an individual this is worse at every step, but advisers still recommend it for inheritance planning and income splitting, so it is shown.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Fixed asset tax of 1.4% a year on the appraised value of real property (plus city planning tax in urban areas, not verified); registration and licence tax 0.1-2% on registration.

inheritance.summary: Inheritance tax is charged on heirs, but computed on the estate: the basic deduction (JPY 30 million + 6 million per statutory heir) is subtracted, the remainder is divided notionally by statutory shares, each share is taxed at progressive rates from 10% to 55% (above JPY 600 million), and the total is allocated to the actual recipients. Gifts are taxed at similar progressive rates (annual exemption JPY 1.1 million per recipient); gifts within 7 years before death are added back. Heirs who are permanent residents, or foreigners with a residence status who have lived in Japan more than 10 of the last 15 years, are taxed on worldwide property (Inheritance Tax Act art. 1-3(1)(i)).
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Basic deduction JPY 30 million + JPY 6 million x number of statutory heirs (Inheritance Tax Act art. 15; NTA No.4152). At the modelled second death (spouse already dead, three children) there are 3 statutory heirs: JPY 48 million in total, JPY 16 million per child; this is the coded exemption per child. (With a surviving spouse, 4 heirs, the total would be JPY 54 million.) Spouse credit (tax-free up to the larger of the statutory share or JPY 160 million; general knowledge, not verified).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Optional inheritance-time settlement gift regime: parents aged 60+ to children aged 18+, 20% flat gift tax above a JPY 25 million lifetime deduction, credited against later inheritance tax. 'Temporary resident' and 'foreign decedent' rules exempt foreign property for foreigners who have lived in Japan 10 years or less in the last 15 (see special regimes).

inheritance.spouse_note: Spouse's tax credit: no tax on the net estate the spouse actually receives up to the greater of JPY 160 million or the spouse's statutory share (half the estate when there are children), provided a return is filed and the estate is divided, or a division-expected form is filed and division follows within 3 years (Inheritance Tax Act art. 19-2; NTA Tax Answer No. 4158). Anything above that is taxed on the normal scale.
inheritance.gift_tax: Progressive gift tax up to 55% above JPY 1.1 million a year per recipient (special lower scale for gifts from parents/grandparents to adult descendants; not detailed), or the elective 20% inheritance-time settlement regime. Gifts within 7 years before death are added to the estate.
inheritance.business_relief: Business succession deferral for unlisted company shares exists (conditions not verified); listed portfolios get no relief.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Worldwide for Japanese nationals domiciled in Japan within the last 10 years and for foreigners beyond the temporary thresholds; only Japan-situs property for temporary foreigners and their heirs.
inheritance.domicile_rules: NTA No.4138: temporary resident = holds a residence status and has lived in Japan 10 years or less in the 15 years before inheritance; foreign decedent = held a residence status and Japanese address at death. Japanese nationals stay in worldwide scope for 10 years after leaving.

regimes.name: Non-permanent resident + temporary foreigner (first 5 years)
regimes.description: A foreign national resident in Japan for 5 years or less in the last 10 is a non-permanent resident: taxed on Japan-source income and on foreign-source income only if paid in or remitted to Japan. During this time (and up to 10 years in the last 15) a foreigner holding a work-type residence status is a 'temporary' person for inheritance tax: foreign property is outside Japanese inheritance and gift tax.
regimes.eligibility: Non-Japanese national with a Japanese domicile; aggregate stay 5 years or less in the previous 10. For inheritance: holder of a residence status listed in Table 1 (work/business-type visas such as Business Manager; not permanent resident or spouse visas) with 10 years or less of residence in the past 15. A non-working family needs a qualifying visa; the Business Manager visa requires running a real business in Japan (requirements not verified).

capital_gains.summary: Non-permanent residents are taxed on income other than foreign-source income, and on foreign-source income paid in Japan or remitted from abroad (Income Tax Act art. 7(1)(ii)). Since the 2017 reform, gains on securities are treated as non-foreign-source (taxed in full regardless of remittance) when the securities were acquired during a period as a non-permanent resident within the 10 years before the sale. Gains on securities acquired BEFORE becoming resident in Japan ('specified securities') are foreign-source when sold on a foreign exchange, through a foreign broker, or from a foreign custody account, and are taxed only if paid in Japan or remitted (Order art. 17(1)). Foreign listed gains are coded at 20.315% because any portfolio turnover after arrival creates fully taxable holdings.

Securities bought while a non-permanent resident are taxed at 20.315% regardless of remittance.

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends paid and kept abroad are not taxed for a non-permanent resident; amounts remitted to Japan are taxed. Japanese dividends as standard.

dividends.eligibility_conditions: Remittance basis: the 0% foreign_gross_rate ASSUMES foreign dividends are paid and kept abroad. Amounts remitted to Japan are taxed (remittances are deemed to come first from other foreign-paid non-foreign-source income, then from foreign-source income, Order art. 17(4)). Dividends paid through a Japanese broker are paid in Japan and fully taxed.

inheritance.summary: While the decedent is a 'foreign decedent' and the heirs are temporary residents, only Japan-situs property is subject to inheritance tax; foreign property (e.g. a portfolio held with a foreign custodian in foreign securities) is outside the charge. Japanese property is taxed on the standard scale.
inheritance.eligibility_conditions: The decedent is a 'foreign decedent': holds a residence status (Table 1 of the Immigration Control Act) and has a Japanese address at death; since the 2021 reform no year count applies to the decedent (Inheritance Tax Act art. 1-3(3)(ii)). Each heir is a 'temporary resident': holds a Table 1 residence status and has lived in Japan 10 years or less in the 15 years before death (art. 1-3(3)(i)); an heir who has passed 10 of 15 years is taxed on worldwide property whoever the decedent was (art. 1-3(1)(i)(a)).

regimes.name: Asset-management company (shisan kanri gaisha: Japanese KK or GK)
regimes.description: The family holds the portfolio through a Japanese company (kabushiki kaisha or godo kaisha) that the parents own. The company is taxed on its worldwide income at the ordinary corporate rates, with no relief for portfolio shares: about 35.43% in total for a small Tokyo company with taxable income above JPY 25 million (national corporate tax 23.2%, local corporate tax 10.3% of it, Tokyo corporate inhabitant tax 10.4% of it, enterprise tax 7.48% plus special corporate enterprise tax of 37% of the 7.0% standard-rate amount, defense special corporate tax 4% of the national tax, enterprise tax deductible when paid). Foreign withholding tax is credited against the national corporate tax. Distributions to the parents are aggregate income, about 49.4% at the top after the dividend credit. Inheritance tax is as for direct holding (the shares are valued at net asset value), so that metric is inherited from the standard regime.
regimes.eligibility: Any resident can found a KK or GK (no minimum capital; notarial deed for a KK, registration). A foreigner needs a residence status that allows running the company (in practice the Business Manager status, with an office and capital or staff requirements that were reportedly tightened in 2025; not verified). Contributing existing shares in kind is a sale at market value for the individual (gain taxed at 20.315%), so the model assumes the company is funded with cash or shares at current cost.
regimes.duration_note: A company under ordinary law with no time limit. Its tax position changes only with the corporate rates and with the 2026 defense special corporate tax, which applies 'for the time being' (Act No. 69 of 2023, art. 9).

structure.entity: Asset-management company (kabushiki kaisha or godo kaisha) held by the parents
structure.payout_notes: Dividends from a Japanese company to a resident shareholder who holds 3% or more, or of an unlisted company, are aggregate income: national tax 45% on the top band (taxable income above JPY 40 million, NTA No.2260) less the dividend credit of 5% of the dividend for the part of taxable income above JPY 10 million (NTA No.1250) = 40%, times 1.021 for the reconstruction surtax = 40.84%; inhabitant tax 10% less the dividend credit of 1.4% (0.6% prefectural + 0.8% municipal for the part above JPY 10 million; Chuo ward page) = 8.6%; total 49.44%. The company withholds 20.42% on the dividend, credited against the shareholder's tax (not verified in the statute). Director's remuneration is deductible for the company but taxed to the director at up to 55.945% and needs real work, which this family does not do; no payout route is cheaper than a dividend.
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: A company with capital of JPY 100 million or less is outside the retained-earnings tax on special family companies (Corporation Tax Act art. 67(1), which carves out companies with capital of JPY 100 million or less other than subsidiaries of large corporations); with a larger capital the tax adds 10%-20% on retained profits above the allowance and the larger enterprise-tax base applies. Art. 132 lets the tax office deny transactions of a family company that reduce tax abnormally. The corporate per-capita inhabitant tax (JPY 70,000 a year or more, PwC) and accounting costs were not sourced and are not counted. No change to the retained-earnings tax was found in the FY2026 reform searches; only art. 67 was read in the statute.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: Liquidation distributions above paid-in capital are deemed dividends (aggregate income). If the parents emigrate, the exit tax (Income Tax Act art. 60-2) covers securities of JPY 100 million or more including the company's shares. At death the shares form part of the estate (valued at net asset value; see the regime's inheritance note).

Unrealised gains are not taxed, and there is no exemption for gains on portfolio holdings.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: National corporate tax 15% on the first JPY 8 million of income for a company with capital of JPY 100 million or less (income up to JPY 1 billion; NTA No.5759); lower Tokyo enterprise-tax bands on the first JPY 8 million. Both are small and the model uses the top rate.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Japanese-resident company. The Tokyo rates apply to an office in the 23 wards; the combined rate elsewhere differs by a point or two.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: The rate is for a company with taxable income above JPY 25 million (Tokyo excess enterprise-tax rates) and national corporate tax above JPY 10 million (corporate inhabitant tax at 10.4%, not 7.0%).

open_questions: Tokyo enterprise-tax rates were read on the Tokyo bureau's page and PwC; the special corporate enterprise tax rate of 37% and the SME bands on the first JPY 8 million rest on PwC only.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Effective statutory rate with enterprise tax deductible when paid: (0.232 x (1 + 0.103 + 0.104) + e) / (1 + e) + 0.04 x 0.232 / (1 + e), where e = 0.0748 + 0.37 x 0.07 = 0.1007 (enterprise tax at the Tokyo excess rate plus special corporate enterprise tax at 37% of the 7.0% standard-rate amount) = 0.3543. This equals the 35.43% 'effective statutory rate' PwC gives for a Tokyo company with capital of JPY 100 million or less. The top marginal rate is used for all income; the 15% national rate on the first JPY 8 million and the lower enterprise-tax bands are ignored.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Not relevant: all company income is taxable profit.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide profits taxed; foreign withholding on dividends is credited against the national corporate tax up to the limit (Corporation Tax Act art. 69).

dividends.summary: Portfolio dividends received by the company are fully taxable at about 35.43% at the top. The 95% exclusion for foreign dividends needs a stake of 25% (PwC) and the exclusion for domestic dividends is 20% for stakes of 5% or less (Corporation Tax Act art. 23(1),(6)). Foreign withholding tax is credited against the national corporate tax (art. 69); the local corporate tax, the defense special corporate tax and the corporate inhabitant tax are computed on the corporate tax before the credit (Local Corporation Tax Act art. 6(1)(i); Act No. 69 of 2023 art. 10; Local Tax Act art. 23(1)(iv)), so the credit offsets only the national tax.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Exclusion of 20% of domestic dividends on stakes of 5% or less; 50% for stakes above 5% and up to one third. None for foreign portfolio dividends.

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain US-taxed; Japan's 20.315% on gains/dividends is creditable against US tax. The US-Japan estate and gift tax treaty coordinates the two inheritance taxes (details not verified). Japanese investment trusts are PFICs.
open_questions: Minimum tax on ultra-high income (22.5% of income above JPY 330 million in 2025-2026; 30% above JPY 165 million from 2027, per PwC) is not reflected in the CGT rates. It is charged only to the extent it exceeds the regular tax, so with a 20.315% regular rate it bites only above roughly JPY 3.4 billion of income in 2026 and roughly JPY 511 million from 2027 (30% x (I - 165m) > 20.315% x I); the reference family (about JPY 100 million of dividends plus gains) is below both. The statute was not opened (PwC only).
Non-permanent residents' foreign securities gains now verified against Income Tax Act art. 7 and Order art. 17 (e-Gov); the treatment of reinvested funds bought before arrival is not confirmed.

Inheritance exemption per child is coded as JPY 16 million: the basic deduction (JPY 30 million + 6 million x 3 statutory heirs = JPY 48 million, Inheritance Tax Act art. 15) at the modelled second death with three children and no surviving spouse. At a first death with a surviving spouse (4 heirs) the total would be JPY 54 million, but the spouse's tax credit then takes the spouse's share, so the children's share is what the engine taxes.
Business Manager visa requirements not verified; cost of living: purchase prices, health insurance and housekeeper wages not sourced.

Valuation of unlisted shares in a family asset-management company for inheritance tax (net asset value less 37% of unrealised gains, Basic Valuation Circular) is not modelled; see the asset_management_kk regime.
